title: Najeon chilgi
summary: Najeon chilgi is Korean lacquerware decorated with thin slivers of shell. A craftsperson saws each petal, leaf or vine from a pearly sheet, beds the pieces into a black lacquered surface and polishes it until the shell glows.
howToPlay: Look at the framed picture: it shows the finished panel.
Trace each outline on the shell sheet with the fretsaw. A piece cut all the way round lifts into the tray.
Drag every piece to its own recess in the black lacquer.
Rub the cloth across the panel until the pearl shines, then press Check.
rules: Three steps: cut, set, polish. Your score is the average of the three.
Cutting is judged on how closely your saw line follows the outline.
Setting is judged on how near each piece lies to its recess; a piece close enough snaps in.
Polishing is judged on how much of the shell you have rubbed clear.
Doing nothing scores nothing. Undo takes back your last cutting stroke.
heritageNote: Najeon chilgi has been made on the Korean peninsula for well over a thousand years. Workshops in Korea still cut, set and polish shell for boxes, chests and small panels, and the craft is passed on from teacher to apprentice.
